column2: pi-jev-model-router: Jev judges the task, code owns the budget — model routing with daily spend caps pi-jev-model-router v0.2.0: One Jev request with 4 parallel questions before every turn: task_kind (Choice), complexity (Score), capability_deserved (Score), needs_deep_reasoning (Noul). Then: demand = 0.55*complexity + 0.45*capability (+ reasoning nudge); demand = max(demand, kind floor) # planning/review never go cheap; confidence guard -> budget guard -> availability guard -> cache guard. "Jev judges the task, code owns the budget." Daily/monthly spend caps auto-downgrade tiers; fails open on missing key/timeout.

SeeAPI: context compaction by filtering — keep, truncate, or exclude context blocks SeeAPI — Jev context compaction: use a fast decision model to keep, truncate, or exclude individual context blocks while leaving retained evidence unchanged. Questions like "Is this result required for the active goal?" / "Does it contain a unique constraint or error?" Hybrid: filter repeatable noise, pin critical evidence verbatim, summarize the narrative core. Caveat: "No official source proves that Jev context compaction improves end-to-end agent success. Treat social compression ratios as hypotheses until reproduced."

browser-use/jev-ultrafast: dynamic action space for browser agents, clicks never touch an LLM browser-use/jev-ultrafast: indexing the live page into a dynamic action space, then asking Jev to pick both the operation and the target element. A small LLM is invoked only for TYPE_TEXT operations. Everything else — click, scroll, select — never touches a generative model.

aidxn: cheap models as always-on watchers — the expensive model thinks, the cheap model stares aidxn.com — cheap models as always-on watchers: "The expensive model does the thinking, the cheap model does the staring." tail -f dev.log | grep -Ei 'error|failed', then a small model reads the matches and answers one question: did anything actually explode. A Haiku-class model does it perfectly and costs a rounding error to leave on all day. Wire it as a notification, not a report.

Maximem: a map of decision seams — where NOT to put a classifier in an agent Maximem — a map of decision seams: "can you write down every possible answer before seeing the input, and does code do something different for each one? If the answer is a sentence, it is not a seam." Warns most disappointment comes from pointing Jev at whole use cases instead of individual seams. 11 seams mapped.

uehaj/herdr-jev-prompt-router: one Jev question routes prompts across workspace panes uehaj herdr-jev-prompt-router: 273-line, zero-dependency TypeScript router. Asks Jev ONE Choice question to decide which of 5-10 open herdr workspaces a prompt should go to, then places the text in that pane's input (does NOT press Enter — human keeps the send decision). "Make criteria keys machine IDs and values the LLM-facing description; the answer comes back usable as a key directly."

classifier.dev smart tier: re-ask only what the model was unsure about classifier.dev smart tier: re-asks only what Jev was unsure about. +2.5 points on AG News (+18.4 on unsure items), +1.0 on emotion (+4.9 on unsure). Jev alone: AG News 87.5% (65.3% unsure); smart tier 90.0% (83.7% unsure). CLI: classify relevant,"not relevant" --review 0.7 < snippets.txt — only the unsure ones re-asked. 1000 lines/request.
